clue.text: Spin on error at 17 or 20? I prepare tall story, if stitch fails badly

indicators.note: the fodder words fail badly, so their letters are thrown into a new order

parts.words: I prepare tall story, if stitch fails

explanation.surface: A seamstress whose stitching keeps failing dresses it up with a tall story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges all thirty letters of I PREPARE TALL STORY IF STITCH FAILS. 17 (AUBUSSON) and 20 (BAYEUX) are famous tapestry towns, so a tapestry maker's spin on a mistake would be this proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb is a shrugging excuse that treats any mishap as just one more thread in the varied weave of existence.

clue.text: Adman's effect a smash hit?

definitions.meaning: the effect an advertisement has on its audience, its punch
a collision, one thing smashing into another

explanation.surface: Is a smash hit the effect every advertising man craves?
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the strong influence of an advert and the physical force of a collision.

clue.text: Typing order to move from the sidelines

definitions.text: Typing order to move from the sidelines

parts.words: Typing order to move from the sidelines
parts.note: an instruction in typing to start a line further in from the margin, read as a player coming in off the touchline

explanation.surface: A coach orders a substitute to come off the bench and join the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting a line in from the margin is the typist's instruction, the margins being the page's sidelines.

clue.text: Plant requiring some paring

indicators.note: read as re-quiring, putting the letters of the following words together again in a new order

explanation.surface: A garden plant that needs a little pruning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'requiring' rearranges SOME PARING; the surface has the plant needing a trim.
explanation.definitionFit: An angiosperm is any flowering plant, one whose seeds develop inside an ovary.

clue.text: The cheek! Psyche has stored fat!

parts.note: lip means cheek, impudence
the id is part of the psyche in Freudian theory

explanation.surface: An outraged exclamation that someone's mind has been hoarding fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipids are the class of fatty organic compounds, including the fats the body stores.

clue.text: Ticked off time after time during retirement?

indicators.note: the time pieces sit during, inside, the word for retirement

parts.note: going to bed is retiring for the night

indicators.note: after places the first time piece behind the second

parts.note: an era is a period of time
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone scolded again and again during their years of retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests old age, but here it means going to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ticked off is to be scolded, the same as being harshly told off.

clue.text: King of Ireland's brother, a Scot born with our failing

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

indicators.note: failing letters collapse and are put back in a different order

explanation.surface: Royal family history: a king's brother, a Scotsman, born with a family weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges OUR to ORU at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Brian Boru was the High King of Ireland killed at the Battle of Clontarf in 1014.

clue.text: See 1 across
Having inside information on the employees, one takes prisoners

parts.note: a tip is a piece of inside information
the staff are the employees

explanation.surface: An insider with knowledge about the workforce turns captor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court officer who takes people into custody, named for the metal-tipped staff carried.

clue.text: Three ducks! Lords playing so sadly

indicators.note: the letters are playing about, changing places

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so three ducks give three Os

explanation.surface: A sad cricket scorecard: three ducks at Lord's ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges OOO and LORDS; 'so' is a link. LORD'S is London's famous cricket ground, where a duck means scoring nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Doloroso is the Italian musical direction to perform sorrowfully, in a sad manner.

clue.text: Poor creature heard on the Melton Mowbray trail?

indicators.note: heard means the phrase is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a dog following the scent of pies: Melton Mowbray is the English market town famous for pork pies

explanation.surface: A hungry animal sniffing its way through a famous pie town.
explanation.walkthrough: MELTON MOWBRAY is a Leicestershire town famous for pork pies, so a dog on its trail is a pie dog, sounding like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pi-dog is a stray, ownerless dog of Asian towns, a pitiable creature.

clue.text: Royal Harry, eh? Abdicating for excessively good return from capital

indicators.note: the letters of eh give up their place, stepping aside for the other piece

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's royal Harry, later Henry V
taken as written

indicators.note: return sends the word for excessively good back to front

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means sanctimoniously good

explanation.surface: Prince Harry gives up the throne in exchange for a good return on his capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns PI into IP, and 'Abdicating for' swaps the EH of PRINCEHAL for it. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal is the capital sum lent or invested, as distinct from the interest earned on it.

clue.text: United teaming commander, sergeant and injured outside right

parts.note: CO is commanding officer
a sergeant is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right goes outside, around, the jumbled word
injured means damaged, so the letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A team line-up: commanding officer, sergeant and a wounded outside right.
explanation.walkthrough: Outside right is an old football position, a red herring: 'outside' wraps the right abbreviation round the injured 'and'.
explanation.definitionFit: Concordant means in agreement or harmony, joined together as one.

clue.text: Dream up?

parts.note: to dream with one's eyes turned upward to the sky at night

explanation.surface: A query about inventing something.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaze at the stars is also an idiom for daydreaming, while literally looking up.

clue.text: This is sick! Ali G's performing among Europeans! Ban it!

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: among puts the shuffled comedian between the two Europeans

parts.note: E stands for European, and two give EE

indicators.note: performing letters act out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An outraged viewer demands that Ali G's act among Europeans be banned.
explanation.walkthrough: Ali G is a British comedian's character, whose name and possessive S together are the fodder for 'performing'.
explanation.definitionFit: To illegalise something is to make it unlawful, which is to ban it.

clue.text: See 1
Tones down on music

parts.note: re means on or about, as in a letter heading
strains are passages of music

explanation.surface: Turning the volume down on some music.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or moderate, much as one tones down something.

clue.text: See 1 across
16 from here to the French Kiss, then forward!

parts.note: au is French for to the
buss is an old word for a kiss
on means forward, as in moving on

explanation.surface: A French romantic getaway: a kiss, then onward.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubusson, a town in central France, has made famous tapestries and carpets for centuries.

clue.text: Reassure cup contenders: no point going in for this treatment

definitions.text: no point going in for this treatment

indicators.note: contenders battle each other, so these letters are fought into a new order

explanation.surface: A sports team is comforted before a cup match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contenders' rearranges REASSURE CUP. Unlike acupuncture, this therapy uses pressure with no needle point going in.
explanation.definitionFit: Acupressure applies finger pressure to the body's points rather than piercing them with needles.

clue.text: Claim what the tipster offers verbally

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a racing tipster offers a cert, a certainty

explanation.surface: A punter hearing a tipster's claim at the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something is to claim it confidently as true.

clue.text: B-Bardot's eyes encompassing a 16 here

indicators.note: the stammered start and the eyes surround, encompass, the next piece

parts.note: a stammered B, then yeux, French for eyes, as Brigitte Bardot is French

explanation.surface: A stammering admirer gazes into Brigitte Bardot's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Brigitte Bardot is a French film star, so her eyes are YEUX; 'encompassing' puts A after the stammered B.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayeux in Normandy is home to the famous embroidered tapestry of the Norman Conquest.

clue.text: Even characters in Centauri make the case

indicators.note: take the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A space mission to Alpha Centauri sets out its argument.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles or cosmetics.

clue.text: Gulf's found here in space, sailor having one solution

indicators.note: the sailor and the rest go in the word for space

parts.note: an area is a space
AB is an able-bodied seaman
I is the Roman numeral one
ANS abbreviates answer, a solution

explanation.surface: A sailor finds his answer somewhere in open space.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gulf of Oman and Gulf of Aden open off the Arabian Sea, part of the Indian Ocean.

clue.text: Instrument to uphold the Simpson arrest

indicators.note: in a down clue holding up means reading the pieces from the bottom upward

parts.note: O. J. Simpson, the American footballer
nab means to arrest

explanation.surface: A court is asked to uphold O. J. Simpson's arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: A banjo is a stringed musical instrument with a drum-like body.

clue.text: See 12
Bad Samaritan losing right to name this devil

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters are rearranged
losing means the letter for right goes and the letter for name takes its place

explanation.surface: A Samaritan gone bad, no longer upright, is named as a devil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing right to name' swaps R for N, giving SAMANITAN, and 'Bad' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasmanian devil is a carnivorous marsupial found in the Australian island state of Tasmania.

clue.text: Heron flew from Robin Hill in dire need

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird flies off a hill in an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: Heron is not a bird but a maiden name: in Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga, Irene, née Heron, left the house at Robin Hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Galsworthy's heroine Irene Forsyte, born Heron, fled her husband Soames and the house at Robin Hill.

clue.text: That old work's conclusion: Queens is in New York!

parts.note: yon is an old word for that

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: ER is the abbreviation for a queen, so two queens give ERS

explanation.surface: Queens is boasted of as part of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Queens suggests the New York borough but supplies queen abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Yonkers is a city in New York State, bordering the Bronx.

clue.text: So might the Chancellor open with a kiss

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: The Chancellor opens proceedings with a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer sets British taxes, so he might charge too much.
explanation.definitionFit: A finance minister who sets taxes too high would burden people unduly.
